transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, things have been a bit complicated lately. I work as a financial advisor, and... I don't know, it sounds strange to say out loud. But for a while now, I've just been pretty convinced that certain people here in Cincinnati—mostly in the arts and finance circles—are... quietly tracking which clients I meet with. 

And they, um... they send me these little signals about it. Just through things like event invitations, or the topics they choose for panels... even who ends up sitting near me at events. I mean... I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence. But... I just can't really let it go.

{"intent": "Assess for auditory hallucinations to differentiate delusional disorder from schizophrenia", "question": "That sounds like a stressful experience to go through. Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you didn't seem to hear
Um... no. I haven't experienced anything like that. Just... what I already told you. I don't hear voices.
Aside from the stress this has caused, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness or depression?
Um... no. Not really. I mean... it's stressful, like you said, but I wouldn't say I'm depressed. Just... trying to manage everything, I guess.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized, euphoric, or on top of the world?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't felt like that. Just... normal, I guess.
About how long have you felt that people have been tracking you and sending you these signals?
Um... I guess it started about... two months ago. Yeah, around two months. That's when I first noticed them, you know, keeping tabs on my client meetings and... doing the signals.
Have you ever felt like thoughts were being placed into your mind from an outside source?
No. I... I don't really know what you mean by that. My thoughts are just my own.
